title: Expedition 33 Guide - Complete Game Guide & Tips
description: Complete Expedition 33 guide covering combat mechanics, exploration, characters, weapons, Pictos, and progression tips for Clair Obscur.

sections.title: Core Systems Overview
sections.content:
Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 combines turn-based RPG strategy with real-time defensive mechanics. Understanding the game's interconnected systems is key to mastering combat and exploring the Continent effectively.

Key Systems

  • Combat: Hybrid turn-based/real-time system where characters act based on Speed, but you react to enemy attacks in real time with Dodge, Jump, Parry, or Counter.
  • Weapons: Each character wields a unique weapon type that scales from D to S rank. Upgrade weapons using Chroma Catalysts found throughout the world.
  • Pictos: Equippable relics providing passive stat boosts and special effects. After 4 battles, a Pictos unlocks its Lumina effect for permanent party-wide assignment.
  • Lumina Points: Earned on level-up, these let you equip unlocked Pictos effects to any character. Stack multiple effects for powerful combinations.
  • Attributes: Each level-up grants 3 points to distribute among Vitality, Might, Agility, Defense, and Luck.
  • Gradient Attacks: Build charge by spending AP (5% per 1 AP spent). These powerful abilities grant a bonus turn after use.

sections.title: Combat Mechanics
sections.content:
Combat in Expedition 33 requires both strategic planning and quick reflexes. Every battle tests your ability to manage AP, exploit weaknesses, and time defensive actions precisely.

Action Points (AP)

AP fuels your skills. Basic attacks and gun shots each cost 1 AP. Managing your AP pool is the difference between a wasted turn and a devastating combo. You can generate extra AP through Parrying (grants +1 AP per successful parry) and specific Pictos like Energising Start and Energising Turn.

Defensive Actions

  • Dodge (B/Circle): Easiest to execute — avoid damage entirely with correct timing.
  • Parry (RB/R1): Harder timing window, but rewards you with +1 AP and a powerful counterattack.
  • Jump (A/X): Required for Jump Flares and certain ground attacks that cannot be dodged.
  • Gradient Counter (RT/R2): Activated when the screen darkens. Counters enemy Gradient Attacks.

Breaking Enemies

The yellow meter beneath an enemy's health bar fills from damage. When full, use multi-hit or Break skills to stun the enemy, skip their turn, and deal increased damage while they're vulnerable. Gustave's Overcharge and Lune's Rockslide are excellent Break tools.

Shields

Shielded enemies must have shields removed before taking real damage. Each gun bullet removes one shield icon. Burn status also removes one shield at turn start. Multi-hit skills like Gustave's Lumiere Assault (5 hits) are particularly effective.

Damage Cap

Damage is limited to 9,999 for most of the story. Once you defeat the final story boss, you unlock the Painted Power Pictos which removes this limit entirely.

sections.title: Exploration Tips
sections.content:
The Continent is vast and rewards thorough exploration with powerful Pictos, weapons, and resources that make your journey significantly easier.

Movement & Mounts

You begin on foot, but eventually gain access to Esquie — a mythical mount that can swim, dive, and eventually fly. Collect Esquie's missing rocks scattered across the world to unlock new traversal abilities. Once you collect 5 Gestrals, you unlock the ability to break Paint Spikes blocking paths throughout the Continent.

Key Exploration Tips

  • Follow the lights to stay on the critical path — lamps always mark the way forward. Unlit paths lead to optional areas.
  • DANGER zones indicate areas above your current level. Return later when you've leveled up.
  • Paint Cages require finding and shooting 3 marked red spots to unlock loot.
  • Petanks run from you — chase them to their matching ground symbol for a puzzle fight.
  • White Nevrons are friendly. Bring them requested items (usually found nearby) for weapon and Pictos rewards.
  • Rest at Expedition Flags to heal, but know it respawns enemies. Use Chroma Elixirs instead to heal without respawning.

Camping

Press D-Down on the world map to camp. Here you can speak with expedition members, upgrade consumables and weapons via the Curator, allocate Lumina points, and build relationships. Reaching relationship level 3 with each party member unlocks a special Gradient Attack.

sections.content:

Each character can equip 6 skills at a time, though you can unlock many more. If your active party of 3 falls in battle, remaining members enter for a Last Stand phase.

sections.title: Progression Tips
sections.content:
Early Game Priorities

  • Collect all prologue items — fight the mime near the shore and get all 3 Festival tokens for vendor purchases.
  • Learn to Parry early. The AP gain and counterattack damage are essential throughout the entire game.
  • Use Chroma Elixirs freely — they fully heal your party and are replenished at every rest point.
  • Set up elemental variety across your party to exploit weaknesses.

Mid Game (Acts 1-2)

  • Prioritize unlocking Pictos Lumina effects by winning 4 battles with each equipped. Don't forget to actually allocate Lumina Points in the menu.
  • Challenge optional bosses for exclusive weapons and Pictos. Chromatic Nevrons are particularly rewarding.
  • Use Maelle at the Gestral Arena — she earns the Medalum weapon, which starts her in Virtuose Stance every fight.
  • Upgrade weapons with Chroma Catalysts at the Curator's camp station.

Late Game & Endgame

  • Once you get Painted Power (removes 9,999 damage cap), equip it on everyone immediately.
  • Stack Energising Start Pictos and AP-generating Luminas for devastating opening turns.
  • The Endless Tower contains the hardest boss fights and best rewards in the game.
  • Build relationships to level 3 with all party members for their unique Gradient Attacks.
